title: The summary for Tuesday 24 November
text:
Good morning, it is Tuesday 24 November: this is the GERICO summary.

We start with Ukraine. A Russian attack on a building in Zaporizhzhia has killed two people and wounded at least twenty-two, according to the head of the regional military administration. Rescuers are still searching for other victims under the rubble. In Dymer, near Kyiv, there are at least eleven dead, and in the region, Ukrainian authorities count at least fifteen.

Still on Ukraine, a piece of news that has not been independently verified: according to the British press, the head of the Pentagon has not yet approved approximately sixty Patriot interceptors already promised to Kyiv. The Pentagon says that the support policy has not changed.

In the Middle East, Iran claims that three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The information comes from the Revolutionary Guards and has no independent confirmation.

In Italy, the subscription period for Intesa Sanpaolo's offer for Monte dei Paschi opens today. For each share, Intesa is offering one euro and twenty-five cents in cash and 1.664 of its own shares. Subscriptions remain open until 22 January.

Let's move to the markets. Yesterday Wall Street closed sharply higher following the return of Jensen Huang to the helm of Nvidia. The Nasdaq gained 6.5%, the S&P 500 4.7% and the Dow Jones 3%. It is the rebound after Friday's collapse.

European stock markets closed in a rally. Frankfurt gained 2.15%, Paris 1.48% and London 1.3%. Piazza Affari rose by 0.65% to 49,021 points: the index was weighed down by the dividend ex-date of eleven companies.

In Asia, Tokyo opened 3% higher this morning, with the Nikkei at 58,159 points, driven by technology and semiconductor stocks.

On the foreign exchange markets, the yen continues to strengthen: the dollar is worth 158.80 yen. For gold, oil and other currencies, we do not have verified data for this morning.

Let's look at today's appointments. At 10:00 the Ifo index on German business confidence arrives, expected at 90.5. At 16:00, in the United States, the Conference Board consumer confidence, expected at 92.4. At 18:25, the Governor of the Bank of Canada, Tiff Macklem, speaks.

The full news, with sources, is on GERICO. No investment advice.
